data.name: Sohrab
data.gender_notes: Sohrab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sohrab means 'lion' in Persian and Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Persian word 'shahrab', which means 'roaring lion'. This powerful and fierce name is a perfect choice for a baby boy, evoking images of bravery and strength. The name Sohrab carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Persian tradition and is also used in Persian, Hindi. Parents who choose Sohrab usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sohrab is a name of a legendary warrior from Persian mythology, who was renowned for his courage and strength. He was the son of Rustam, a great hero in Persian legend, and Tahmine, a princess from the rival kingdom of Turan. The name Sohrab symbolizes the power and strength of the divine lion, and is a reminder of the courage and determination needed to overcome adversity and face challenges in life.
data.etymology: Sohrab belongs to the Persian linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sohrab total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sohrab" has a rich cultural significance, particularly in Hindu and Persian mythology. In Hindu mythology, there is a famous tale of a brave king named Rustam, who had a son named Sohrab. Rustam, who was considered a fierce warrior and a champion of good, had his son Sohrab raised in the forest away from his court to ensure his son's safety. This happened because Rustam had a prophecy that his son would kill him in battle. However, destiny had its own plan, and when Sohrab grew up, he and Rustam ultimately fought each other in a fierce battle, with Sohrab emerging victorious. This tragic but inspiring story of a father and son has been passed down for generations and highlights the power and innocence of youth, as well as the complexities of destiny and the cavalier nature of war.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Sohrab" carries with it a deep spiritual significance, symbolizing raw strength and courage. In Hinduism, the lion is considered the king of all animals and represents power, courage, strength, and royalty. In Persian mythology, the lion is also a symbol of the warrior and the brave. Therefore, the name Sohrab, which literally means 'roaring lion', symbolizes the inner power and courage that lies within each and every one of us. It is a reminder to stand up for what is right, to face our fears head-on, and to approach life with a fierce determination and unwavering strength. Ultimately, the name Sohrab is a beautiful reminder of the infinite potential that resides within each of us, waiting to roar.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sohrab in Hinduism represents the indomitable spirit and courage of young warriors. Named after the legendary hero Sohrab from the Persian epic "The Story of Rostam and Sohrab," this name symbolizes the deep bond between a father and son, and the sacrifices one makes for love and honor.
